title: Canonical rigidified ample line module on smooth relative Jacobians
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $g\geq2$, and let $C\to S$ be a smooth stable unpointed genus-$g$ family [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose $J=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/S}$, the degree-zero part of the relative Picard fppf sheaf [sk-def-picard-pic], is represented by an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The canonical principal polarization of this Jacobian defines a line module $B(C/S)$ on $J$, with a specified identity-section trivialization $e^*B(C/S)\simeq\mathcal O_S$. It is symmetric under inversion and relatively ample. Here a line module is an $\mathcal O_J$-module on its small etale site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_J$; relatively ample means that $J$ is a scheme and the corresponding ordinary invertible module is ample on the inverse image of each affine open of $S$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The normalization is the diagonal Poincare normalization: if $\lambda_C:J\to J^\vee$ is the canonical theta principal polarization and $\mathcal P$ is the Poincare module on $J\times_SJ^\vee$ trivialized on both identity axes, then $B(C/S)=(1,\lambda_C)^*\mathcal P$. Here $J^\vee$ represents line modules algebraically trivial on geometric fibres, rigidified at the identity, and $\lambda_C$ is the polarization induced by the degree-$(g-1)$ effective-divisor theta class. There are canonical identifications $B(C/S)|_{S'}\simeq B(C_{S'}/S')$ under every base change of locally Noetherian schemes and under every isomorphism of curve families. These identifications preserve the identity trivialization and satisfy identity and composition, including on triple fibre products.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-jacobian-theta-polarization] to obtain the proper smooth group space $J$ and its theta isomorphism $\lambda_C:J\to J^\vee$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus], its normalized universal module $\mathcal P$ exists. Put $d=(1,\lambda_C)$ and $B=d^*\mathcal P$. Pullback of a locally free rank-one module is locally free rank one: in local frames it is the tensor pullback of $\mathcal O$ and hence $\mathcal O$. Since $d e=(e,e^\vee)$, the compatible axis trivializations give the specified $e^*B\simeq\mathcal O_S$. This is exactly the required diagonal normalization, without choosing a global theta representative.

source.place: §4.1, printed p.141, diagonal construction and identity normalization

proof.text: Biadditivity and the zero-axis trivializations in [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus] give $\mathcal P(-x,y)\simeq\mathcal P(x,y)^{-1}$ and $\mathcal P(x,-y)\simeq\mathcal P(x,y)^{-1}$ as families: substitute $x+(-x)=0$ or $y+(-y)=0$ in the displayed tensor identities and cancel. Applying both gives $(-1,-1)^*\mathcal P\simeq\mathcal P$. As $\lambda_C(-x)=-\lambda_C(x)$, pull back along $d$ to get $[-1]^*B\simeq B$, preserving the identity trivialization.

Fix a geometric point $\bar s$ with field $K$. By [lem-sfb-relative-jacobian-theta-polarization], $J_K$ is an abelian variety and $\lambda_K=\phi_L$ for an ample theta module $L$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus], $N_L=(1\times\phi_L)^*\mathcal P_K$. Restrict this identity along $x\mapsto(x,-x)$. Its right side is $B_K^{-1}$ by biadditivity in the second variable; its left side is $L^{-1}\otimes[-1]^*L^{-1}\otimes\pi^*(e^*L)^{\otimes2}$, where $\pi:J_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Thus $B_K\simeq L\otimes[-1]^*L\otimes\pi^*(e^*L)^{-2}$. Choosing a basis of the one-dimensional $K$-line $e^*L$ removes the last factor. The tensor is ample by [lem-sc-ample-tensor]. This proves ampleness on every geometric fibre, with no assumption that 2 is invertible.

source.place: §4.1, printed pp.141--142, ampleness; normalized difference-family computation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-ample-locus] to the proper space $J\to S$ and $B$. The preceding calculation shows that every geometric fibre is in its ample locus $A\subseteq S$, so $A=S$. Its conclusion gives that $J$ is a scheme and that $B$ is ample over every affine open of $S$, exactly the relative ampleness in the item.

proof.text: For $v:S'\to S$, the Picard and theta identifications of [lem-sfb-relative-jacobian-theta-polarization] identify $d_{C_{S'}}$ with $d_C\times_SS'$. The universal-module comparison of [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus], pulled back along this graph, gives $v_J^*B(C/S)\simeq B(C_{S'}/S')$. For $u:C\simeq D$, put $a=(u^{-1})^*:J_C\simeq J_D$. The identity $a^\vee\lambda_Da=\lambda_C$ and $(a\times1)^*\mathcal P_D\simeq(1\times a^\vee)^*\mathcal P_C$ give $a^*B(D/S)\simeq B(C/S)$ by substitution on the graph. All comparisons preserve the identity trivialization. On a composite base change or family isomorphism, the direct comparison and the composite comparison are maps between the same rigidified line modules. Their quotient is an identity-rigidified automorphism on the proper abelian space $J$, which is the identity by the universal rigidity assertion of the Poincare node. Hence identities and composition hold, also on triple fibre products.
